paper_sections.title: Ghrelin Modulates Brain Activity in Areas that Control Appetitive Behavior

description.value: The study examined whether intravenous ghrelin modulates neural responses to food pictures relative to scenery pictures in healthy nonobese men, and whether these neural effects relate to hunger and recognition of food cues.

design.value: Twenty healthy medication-free normal-weight male subjects underwent a single fMRI session 3 hr after a standardized breakfast. Twelve subjects viewed food and scenery pictures before and after ghrelin administration, while eight subjects viewed the same paradigm in two control blocks without ghrelin to assess order effects.

description.value: Subjects answered questions regarding their mood and appetite, including how hungry they were, at the start and end of each block.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Screening Module

description.value: The eating-related section was used to exclude potential subjects with abnormal eating behavior.

Approximately 30 min after scanning, subjects were shown the 45 food images viewed in the scanner intermixed with 26 novel food images and stated whether they had seen each image while in the scanner.
Subjects rated the images on a scale of 1 to 9, with 1 indicating extremely dislike and 9 indicating extremely like.

source_definition.value: Separate regressors for food and scenery pictures were included in the general linear model.
The interaction between the control/ghrelin group and the control/control group was examined.
The interaction effect was calculated as ([ghrelin − control] − [control 2 − control 1]).
Scenery images were contrasted to the blank screen stimulus to ensure that ghrelin did not alter the response to scenery pictures nonspecifically.

The fMRI signal, the effect size from the general linear model, in the food minus scenery contrast was correlated with self-report measures; the increase in activation due to ghrelin correlated with self-reported hunger during the ghrelin scans.
Right insula activation correlated positively with recognition scores for the ghrelin pictures.

task_name.value: food and scenery picture viewing paradigm

task_description.value: During each functional run, 15 images, consisting of 7–8 food and 7–8 scenery images, were presented in random order. Each picture was shown for 5 s followed by a 15 s dark screen with a central fixation cross. The first and second blocks each consisted of three 5 min functional runs.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (version 9.60, Neurobehavioral Systems, CA, USA)

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to focus their attention on the stimuli.

stimuli.value: Food and scenery pictures, previously matched for visual appeal; 45 images were displayed in the first block, consisting of 22 food and 23 scenery images, and 45 different images were displayed in the second block, consisting of 23 food and 22 scenery images.

task_performance_measures.value: hunger and mood ratings on a 10 point visual analog scale
recognition of food images viewed in the scanner
hedonic ratings of the images on a scale of 1 to 9

modality.value: T2* weighted images with BOLD contrast

instrument.value: 1.5T Siemens Vision MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature radiofrequency head coil

description.value: Thirty-two 4 mm thick slices that covered the whole brain were collected. The functional session consisted of six runs of 5 min, each consisting of 100 volumes per run. Scanning time and stimulus presentation were synchronized by a trigger signal from the scanner at the beginning of every run. Two dummy images were taken at the onset of each sequence and discarded to reduce non-steady state effects.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2* weighted images with BOLD contrast

instrument.value: 1.5T Siemens Vision MRI scanner equipped with a quadrature radiofrequency head coil

description.value: Following breakfast and before functional scanning, high-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images were obtained.

Functional images were spatially smoothed with a 6 mm Gaussian filter and motion corrected prior to statistical analyses. Parametric images were transformed into Montreal Neurological Institute space.

steps.value: spatially smoothed with a 6 mm Gaussian filter
parametric images transformed into Montreal Neurological Institute space

model_settings.value: Separate regressors for food and scenery pictures, consisting of boxcar functions convolved with a standard hemodynamic response function. Regional brain activation was determined by calculating a contrast of food minus scenery and computing effect and standard deviation at each brain voxel for each individual.

estimator.value: t statistic from the effect size and standard deviation of the general linear model for each individual

model_settings.value: Individual parametric images were transformed into Montreal Neurological Institute space and a group analysis was performed using a mixed effects statistical model. The search volume was the entire brain; regions were listed when they contained clusters with p < 0.001 and a volume greater than 100 ml.

model_type.value: t map of the interaction effect

model_settings.value: The interaction between the ghrelin/control group and the control/control group was generated using the effect ([ghrelin − control] − [control 2 − control 1]).
Behavioral and hormonal data were analyzed using SPSS. A paired t test was used to compare these measures in the ghrelin and control conditions.

interpretations.value: The t value at each voxel is a measure of the likelihood that there was greater BOLD signal in response to the food than the scenery pictures at that location in the brain.

definition.value: food minus scenery for control 1 and control 2 combined

interpretations.value: Neural activation associated with food stimuli was examined via subtraction of the scenery response.

definition.value: food minus scenery for all scans, ghrelin and control combined

interpretations.value: Ghrelin increased the response to food pictures in regions of the brain, including the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula, and striatum.

definition.value: food minus scenery in the saline control conditions

interpretations.value: No significant activation in the amygdala, insula, pulvinar, hippocampus, caudate, or OFC was observed in either control condition.
